title: Fix aggregation-window skew causing duplicate credits on mid-cycle invoices
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary:
A subset of mid-cycle invoices have been credited twice for burst quota adjustments. Root cause appears to be a skew between the hourly aggregation window used by the usage rollup job and the export window used by the Stripe/NetSuite reconciler. The rollup was inclusive on window end while the export expected an exclusive end boundary, combined with a non-idempotent export key that allowed the same adjustment to be exported twice across a retry boundary.

Observed behavior:
- Duplicate credit line items appear on NetSuite invoice adjustments for ~0.2% of customers during months with high burst usage.
- Issue correlates with billing-rollup runs overlapping hour boundaries when autoscaler-induced burst occurs near hour ticks.
- Grafana panel billing.exports.credit_rate shows a spike in duplicate credit exports coincident with retried reconciler jobs.

Impact:
- Incorrect customer invoices (over-crediting and subsequent adjustments) and accounting discrepancies requiring manual journal entries to reconcile NetSuite.
- Potential revenue leakage and increased Ops support work.

Hypothesis / technical root cause:
1) Hourly rollup aggregator used inclusive interval semantics (start <= t <= end) while downstream export used half-open semantics (start <= t < end). This led to the same usage bucket being returned in two adjacent aggregation runs in edge cases.
2) Exporter used an export-key based only on (account_id, bucket_timestamp) but did not include a canonical run_id or checksum, meaning retried exports (due to network flakes or partial failures) could be applied twice if the target system accepted them as distinct.
3) Proration allocator applied mid-cycle burst credits by re-splitting invoice lines without idempotent markers, creating duplicate credit lines when fed the same input twice.

Proposed solution:
- Correct aggregator semantics to use half-open intervals consistently across rollup and export (start <= t < end). Add unit tests for boundary conditions including DST transitions and leap seconds.
- Make export pipeline idempotent: include export_checksum and run_id in export key; ensure reconciler checks existing export_keys in NetSuite/Stripe metadata before creating credits.
- Update proration allocator to emit deterministic line ids and detect duplicate adjustments locally before export.
- Implement a safety gate for the next scheduled export: if duplicate-credit rate > 0.05% for the last 24h, pause automated exports and notify Finance/Support.
- Create a backfill/repair job to detect invoices with duplicated credit memos and either consolidate or emit offsetting adjustments; produce a reconciliation report for Finance to approve before NetSuite writes.

Acceptance criteria (see Acceptance Criteria section):
acceptance_criteria: Aggregator adjusted to half-open interval semantics and covered by unit/integration tests for boundary conditions
Exporter produces idempotent export_keys including export_checksum and run_id
Proration allocator emits deterministic line ids and de-duplicates local duplicates
Backfill job identifies affected invoices, produces reconciliation draft, and runs without creating additional duplicates
Monitoring: Grafana alert for duplicate-credit-rate triggers below threshold for 72 hours post-deploy
Finance-approved reconciliation report generated and NetSuite adjustments applied

2026-02-26 - Diego Martínez: Reproduced locally — wrote a small simulation that demonstrates inclusive vs half-open window duplication at the hour boundary. Filing a short RFC to standardize interval semantics across rollup/export services.

2026-03-01 - Diego Martínez: Design review with @Samir Patel (Billing), @Lina Gomez (Finance). Decided to adopt half-open semantics and add export checksums. Lina requested a reconciliation draft before applying any backfill to production NetSuite. See design doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1billing-rfc-57342

2026-03-03 - Diego Martínez: Implemented aggregator fix in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/billing/compare/fix/window-semantics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4528). Added unit tests that exercise minute-level boundaries and DST changeover. CI green locally.

2026-03-05 - QA: Ran integration test against a staging export sink that emulates NetSuite idempotency behavior. Found exporter still created duplicate exports when the checksum algorithm used unstable JSON serialization order. Action: canonicalize serialization and include field ordering in checksum calculation.

2026-03-07 - Diego Martínez: Updated exporter to use canonical JSON (sorted keys) before SHA256 checksum. Added run_id and export_checksum to export_key. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/4536
2026-03-09 - Finance (Lina Gomez): Requested backfill plan and sample reconciliation output for approval before any writes to production NetSuite. Shared sample draft in Confluence.

2026-03-10 - Diego Martínez: Implemented backfill job prototype that flags affected invoices and generates a CSV reconciliation for Finance review. Backfill run is currently read-only in staging. Job link: gs://redwood-billing-backfills/ENG-57342/staging-run-20260310.csv

2026-03-12 - PM (Rohan Iyer): Approved gating thresholds and rollout plan. Plan: deploy aggregator + exporter changes to staging, run backfill in staging, get Finance sign-off, then deploy to prod during maintenance window with export gating enabled. Post-deploy monitor period 72 hours.
